sanskrit: setusnānena ca tathā na tulyaṃ vidyate kvacit | tatsetumūlaṃ laṃkāyāṃ yatrarāmo yiyāsayā || 100 || vānaraiḥ setumārebhe puṇyaṃ pāpa praṇāśanam | taddarbhaśayanaṃ nāmnā paścāllokeṣu viśrutam || 101 || evamuktaṃ mayā viprāḥ samudre setubaṃdhanam | atra tīrthānyanekāni saṃti puṇyānyanekaśaḥ || 102 ||
english: 97b-102. Resorting to this Setu built by Rāma, all men who have committed sins, are liberated from their sins. Śiva is not pleased so much with Vratas, charitable gifts, penances and Homas, as he is pleased with the holy plunge at Setu. Just as there is no other splendour comparable to the refulgence of the Sun, so also there is nothing equal to the holy bath at Setu. A tip of Setu is in Laṅkā where Rāma desired to go and therefore began the construction by the monkeys. It (the tip of Setu) is meritorious and destructive of sins. Afterwards it became well-known by the name Darbhaśayana. Thus, O Brāhmaṇas, the construction of Setu has been recounted by me. There are many meritorious Tīrthas here.
